item: Row J: the curated stamp writes through one UPDATE per chunk and one INSERT
summary: stamp_curated_catalog wrote three attributes per row through the ORM and added one attempt row each (one INSERT statement per row on a first install). It now issues one ORM-enabled bulk UPDATE per 400-id chunk (update(Source) through session.execute), guarded by status = 'unqualified' so a row another writer moved after the scan is neither overwritten nor given an attempt row, and one executemany INSERT of the attempt rows. The rows left are identical to the ORM form column for column (tests/test_curated_stamp_batched.py keeps the old form as the reference). The ORM form also rewrote feed_key from rss_url on every row it touched, through the J1 before_update mapper event, which a bulk UPDATE does not fire: the stamp now repairs a stored key that disagrees with its own rss_url for the rows it stamps, with the same function applied to the rss_url the row holds when it is stamped (re-read inside the write window: the scan's copy can be stale if another writer edits the feed between the scan and the first UPDATE, which an independent read reproduced and a test now pins), in one executemany by primary key and nothing on a healthy store. Bulk DML through session.execute still reaches do_orm_execute, so the single-writer gate and write marker see both statements. Export measured the function before the heal's re-read inside the write window (`keyword-export/stamp-curated-remeasure-2026-10-17/REPORT.md` section 8; that figure is not quoted), then on the final head: Export's clean re-run on `ee373ebed` (`keyword-export/catalogue-parse-remeasure-1430-2026-10-17/clean-rerun/CLEAN-REPORT.md` section 3; nothing else running, 4 shared vCPUs, warm runs, the old per-row stamp and the new one alternating in one session): 0.906 s to 0.176 s per call (-81 %) on a plain store and 0.944 s to 0.186 s (-80 %) on an encrypted one; statements 19 SELECT + 6,616 single INSERTs to 2 SELECT + 17 UPDATE + 1 INSERT executemany; the stored rows' digests are identical between the old and the new form in each store. A store whose keys differ pays about 0.05 to 0.13 s more, once (one run per pass, plain only). The first call in a process still pays about 1 s of catalogue parse, with or without the change. Not probed: a stored key that is non-blank and wrong, and the heal on an encrypted store.
